hints: Look closely at each photomicrograph and compare the dark cell contents with the pale cell wall. Which sample has the protoplast pulled right away into small balls, and which sample has cells completely full with no gaps?

Remember water always moves by osmosis from higher water potential (dilute solution) to lower water potential (concentrated salt solution). Link the degree of plasmolysis to position on the P to R scale.
walkthrough:
**Observe what the cells look like**

Look side by side at X, Y and Z. Sample Y shows severe plasmolysis, the vacuole and cytoplasm have shrunk into small dark rounded balls away from the cell wall with large white gaps.

Sample Z shows the opposite, cells are full, plump and turgid with the dark contents pushing right up to the walls. Sample X is in between, with slight shrinkage.

**Apply osmosis to explain the differences**

In a concentrated salt solution (low water potential), water leaves the onion cells by osmosis, so the protoplast shrinks. This is plasmolysis.

In distilled water or very dilute salt (high water potential), water enters the cells by osmosis, so they become turgid and full.

**Match samples to P, Q and R on the scale**

P is closest to distilled water, so it is the most dilute. R is closest to concentrated salt solution, so it is the most concentrated. Q is in the middle.

Therefore Y (most plasmolysed) must be R, Z (most turgid) must be P, and X (intermediate) must be Q. That is sample Y = R and sample Z = P.

options.A: Incorrect. P is the most dilute solution, but Y is strongly plasmolysed so it cannot be in dilute solution. Z is turgid so it cannot be Q.
options.B: Incorrect. Z is fully turgid with no plasmolysis, so it was not in the very concentrated solution R. Y is correct as R, but Z is wrong.
options.C: Incorrect. Y shows extreme plasmolysis, more than X, so it cannot be only the intermediate Q. Z shows full turgidity, so it cannot be R.
options.D: Correct. Y shows the most water loss and plasmolysis, matching the most concentrated solution R. Z shows full turgid cells, matching the most dilute solution P.
